To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
cortical thickness is systematically related to cortical cytoarchitecture, and that this relationship is modulated by the structural hierarchy of cortical areas.

(i) cortical thickness gradients are systematically related to the structural hierarchical organization of the cortex, (ii) this pattern is similar in two species, macaque and human, (iii) the pattern is not due to cortical folding, (iv) the pattern is similar in the three sensory modalities studied (visual, auditory and somatosensory).
the thickness of the cortex is correlated with cytoarchitectonic characteristics and that the thickness gradients mirror the hierarchical organization of the cortex.
